briefing.opening: Good morning, everyone. I will now begin the climate briefing for August 5, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Extreme Weather Phenomena and Domestic and International Emergency Responses
sections.content: Today, the Korean Peninsula is experiencing 'climate polarization,' simultaneously facing heavy rainfall in the central region and severe drought in the southern region [1, 25]. In the Seoul metropolitan area, including Seoul, extreme heat approaching 39 degrees Celsius has persisted for two days, leading to the issuance of a severe heatwave warning. There are warnings that this could be a precursor to a 'super El Niño' [3, 30, 31, 128]. Due to this heatwave, crop yields are plummeting, leading to soaring prices for spinach and young radish, raising concerns about 'heatflation' [127]. In industrial settings, workers are collapsing from heat-related illnesses [129]. Furthermore, complex crisis situations due to climate change are intensifying, with fire risk warnings being elevated to 'severe' nationwide [133]. This aligns with international reports indicating that climate change is causing disasters such as housing value losses, wildfires, and torrential rains globally [141, 147, 154, 157].

sections.title: 🌱 Climate Change Adaptation and Carbon Neutrality Implementation Efforts
sections.content: Amidst this crisis, various efforts to respond to climate change are actively underway both domestically and internationally. Domestically, a legal framework has been established for climate crisis response and carbon neutrality implementation in agriculture and rural areas, providing a basis for farmers to trade carbon reduction credits [16, 17, 26, 42, 50, 56]. Furthermore, Hanwha E&C has introduced 'NextFlow,' a customized landscaping solution to combat heatwaves [8, 14, 15, 20], and Cheongju City is exploring climate change adaptation in the agricultural sector by cultivating subtropical crops [12]. Korea Water Resources Corporation (K-water) is strengthening its international response capabilities by operating an emergency water supply system to counter climate-induced droughts and expanding digital water management cooperation with five Mekong countries [21, 22, 28]. Education and citizen participation are also active: Siheung Eco Center has prepared experiential education programs for carbon neutrality [11], and various local governments, including Incheon and Daejeon, are promoting campaigns for everyday carbon neutrality practices such as using reusable cups, upcycling, and activating bicycle paths [35, 36, 37, 47, 49, 51, 52, 55, 59, 72, 74, 78, 83].

sections.title: 🌱 Expansion of Renewable Energy and Transition to a Carbon-Neutral Economy
sections.content: The expansion of renewable energy is emerging as a key task for achieving carbon neutrality goals and responding to the climate crisis. Representative Park Hee-seung has sponsored the 'Special Act on Renewable Energy Self-Sufficient Cities,' promoting balanced regional development and the institutionalization of renewable energy supply cooperation zones in the RE100 era [84, 99, 104]. Siheung City is encouraging citizen and corporate participation in renewable energy by producing 'Siheung-type RE100' leaflets [86, 106, 115, 118, 119, 121]. In Songdo, Incheon, '2026 Green Enertech' has opened, presenting a future vision for the environmental and new and renewable energy industries and providing a platform for inter-corporate exchange [85, 92, 93, 94, 98, 100, 103, 108, 109, 111, 120, 122, 124]. Minister of Climate Kim Sung-hwan emphasized that expanding renewable energy is crucial for future competitiveness to overcome both the AI revolution and the climate crisis [97]. Major corporations like Samsung and SK are also raising expectations for renewable energy procurement for their Yongin fabs [113]. However, challenges still remain in expanding renewable energy, as solar power generation this year has fallen significantly short of its annual target [91]. There are also analyses suggesting that carbon neutrality is intensifying beyond a mere environmental issue into a competition for industrial hegemony [38, 43, 73].

sections.title: 🌍 Global Climate Threats and Widespread Impacts
sections.content: Climate change is having widespread global impacts and posing new threats. The European Central Bank (ECB) has warned that climate change threatens the global economy even amidst a surging stock market [152], and internationally, there is a growing call for climate action to be continuously included on the global agenda [148]. In the ecosystem sector, approximately one-tenth of the world's butterfly species have already experienced changes in their geographical range and altitude due to climate change, which is being interpreted as a 'warning signal' [137, 156]. The UK Parliament's Environmental Audit Committee is calling for a review of pet parasiticides, also drawing attention to the indirect impacts of climate change on wildlife [144, 155]. Thus, climate change poses severe threats across the economy, society, and ecosystems, extending beyond mere meteorological phenomena, and comprehensive, all-encompassing responses are urgently needed.

briefing.closing: This concludes today's climate briefing. In this era of climate crisis, our efforts for a sustainable future are becoming increasingly important. Thank you.
